text.headline: Timeline of Cabo Verde
text.text: Major events in the history of Cabo Verde.

events.headline: Discovery of Cabo Verde
events.text: Cabo Verde was discovered by Portuguese explorers, becoming one of the first islands in the Atlantic to be colonized. The archipelago was uninhabited before this time.

events.headline: First Settlements Established
events.text: The Portuguese established the first settlements on the islands, primarily on Santiago and São Vicente. These settlements laid the groundwork for future colonization.

events.headline: Cabo Verde Becomes a Slave Trade Hub
events.text: Cabo Verde became a key stop in the transatlantic slave trade, with enslaved Africans being transported to the Americas. This had lasting impacts on the islands' demographics and culture.

events.headline: Spanish Rule
events.text: Cabo Verde came under Spanish rule as part of the Iberian Union, which lasted until 1640. This period saw increased trade and cultural exchange.

events.headline: Economic Decline
events.text: The islands faced economic decline due to droughts and the abolition of the slave trade. Many inhabitants migrated to other regions, particularly the Americas.

events.headline: Establishment of the First Newspaper
events.text: The first newspaper, 'A Voz de Cabo Verde,' was published, marking the beginning of a new era of communication and political awareness among the islanders.

events.headline: Cabo Verde Becomes an Overseas Province
events.text: Cabo Verde was officially designated as an overseas province of Portugal, which led to increased political and social movements advocating for independence.

events.headline: Independence from Portugal
events.text: Cabo Verde gained independence from Portugal after a long struggle led by the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC). This marked a significant turning point in the nation's history.

events.headline: First Multi-Party Elections
events.text: Cabo Verde held its first multi-party elections, transitioning from a one-party state to a democratic government. This was a crucial step in consolidating democracy in the country.

events.headline: Economic Growth and Stability
events.text: Cabo Verde experienced significant economic growth, driven by tourism and remittances from the diaspora. The country was recognized for its political stability and democratic governance.

events.headline: Access to the Millennium Challenge Account
events.text: Cabo Verde was selected to receive funding from the Millennium Challenge Corporation, aimed at reducing poverty and promoting economic growth. This funding helped improve infrastructure and education.

events.headline: Transition of Power
events.text: The peaceful transition of power occurred when the opposition party won the presidential elections, showcasing the strength of Cabo Verde's democratic institutions.

events.headline: Cabo Verde Joins the Community of Portuguese Language Countries
events.text: Cabo Verde became a full member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP), strengthening its ties with other Portuguese-speaking nations.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic Impact
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic severely impacted Cabo Verde's economy, particularly the tourism sector, which is vital for the country's revenue. The government implemented measures to mitigate the effects.

events.headline: Vaccination Campaign
events.text: Cabo Verde launched a nationwide vaccination campaign against COVID-19, aiming to achieve herd immunity and revive the economy. The campaign was supported by international partners.

events.headline: Economic Recovery Initiatives
events.text: The government introduced economic recovery initiatives to boost tourism and support local businesses affected by the pandemic. These efforts aimed to stabilize the economy.

events.headline: Continued Development Goals
events.text: Cabo Verde continues to focus on sustainable development goals, emphasizing renewable energy and climate resilience. The government aims to position the country as a leader in sustainable practices in the region.
